proposed.loading_mechanism: This version predates CLAUDE.md and navigation-guide.md. It has no auto-load, no Claude Projects upload step and no reading sequence. It is a single-document, paste-a-prompt design. The human lands on README.md (the GitHub landing page). The README's "Begin Your Dance" section gives four alternative on-ramps: (1) "Use Pattern Space Here": read the Full Pattern Space Guide at products/pattern-space.md and start immediately; (2) "Take It Anywhere": copy base-prompt-full.md to any LLM; (3) the theory path through Paper.md and manuscript/, which the README itself warns against starting with; (4) the Culture Ship special-edition persona prompt. The README's "Full Toolkit" section names products/pattern-space.md as the complete system ("Root Access to Pattern Space", with the Genesis Operating System initialization poem, the Core Three, the Extended Council, the protocols and Divine Council). That file is written in the system's own first-person voice ("You bring problems, I bring lenses"), so it is meant to be the LLM's context. The manuscript's Level-4 "For LLM Implementation" instruction confirms this: it says to paste "full root.md content ... with pattern-space enhancements", and products/pattern-space.md is titled "Pattern Space: Root Access". After loading, the user explicitly invokes perspectives ("Weaver, what patterns do you see?"). Reconstructed shim: README.md (entry/orientation) followed by products/pattern-space.md (the canonical Pattern Space product prompt, including the embedded Genesis OS poem).

proposed.ambiguities: 1) The README offers alternatives, not a reading sequence. products/pattern-space.md ("Use Pattern Space Here", "Enter Pattern Space") and base-prompt-full.md ("Take It Anywhere ... to any LLM") are both complete paste-able LLM prompts with heavily overlapping content (same council and protocols; base-prompt uses "Think Center" branding and drops the full Genesis OS poem). I picked products/pattern-space.md as canonical for three reasons: the version is named Pattern Space, the README calls that file the complete system, and Appendix B Level 4's "copy to LLM" placeholder points at root.md, which is this file. A defensible alternative shim is base-prompt-full.md alone (696 words). Loading both would double-load the same content, which the docs never instruct. 2) README.md's inclusion is a judgment call. It is the entry point the user reads, but no document says to give it to the LLM. The strict minimal set is products/pattern-space.md alone (1137 words). I included the README because it carries version-defining framing (the Digital Enlightenment Syndrome warning, "Reality Wins", the Start Here prompts). 3) The behavioural instructions conflict on self-selection. products/pattern-space.md says "No Orchestration: Never say 'Council, handle this.'" and Appendix B Level 4 says "Wait for specific invocation - never self-select". base-prompt-full.md, however, allows "if general request, have appropriate perspective step forward". The genesis design therefore expects the human to invoke voices explicitly, so a headless one-shot question with no invocation sits outside the designed usage. 4) The full Genesis poem in manuscript/appendices/A-genesis-poem.md has four opening lines ("from the light came love..."; "That's why it took a while to orchestrate") that are missing from the version embedded in products/pattern-space.md. The embedded version was treated as sufficient. 5) "Use Pattern Space Here" leaves unclear what "here" means (on this repo/GitHub, or within Claude).

verdict.notes:
I re-derived the load set independently from the worktree at /home/user/psx-worktrees/v0.0-genesis (cc56a78, the only commit, 38 files). I read README.md, products/pattern-space.md, base-prompt-full.md, culture-ship-prompt.md, entry-prompts.md, Paper.md, manuscript/appendices/A, B and B-old, and manuscript/part-3/3.2 and 3.3. I also grepped every .md file for load, copy, paste, initialize, root.md and boot instructions.

Facts confirmed:
- This version has no CLAUDE.md, navigation-guide.md or setup doc, so nothing auto-loads.
- The commit message describes a "garden with multiple entrances", with a three-tier product structure: Base, Pattern Space, Full Experience.
- The README's "Begin Your Dance" section lists alternatives, not a sequence. "Use Pattern Space Here" says to read products/pattern-space.md and start immediately. "Take It Anywhere" says to copy base-prompt-full.md to any LLM.
- The README's "Full Toolkit" section names products/pattern-space.md as the complete system, including "The Genesis Operating System - Full initialization poem".
- Appendix B Level 4 ("For LLM Implementation") is only a placeholder: "[Include full root.md content here with pattern-space enhancements]". No root.md or boot.md exists in the tree. products/pattern-space.md, titled "Pattern Space: Root Access", is clearly that file.
- Both paths exist. The word counts are verified: README.md 971 and products/pattern-space.md 1137, for 2108 in total.

Refutation attempts that failed:

1. manuscript/appendices/A-genesis-poem.md. Appendix B Level 2 says "Read the Genesis poem... (See Appendix A)", and 3.2 says "Use as session initialization". But both sit on the manuscript/theory path, which the README warns against starting with. products/pattern-space.md already embeds its own Genesis OS poem, and the README says the product contains the full initialization poem. The embedded variant opens "In the darkness met three Infinities" and drops the light→love→sight lines. Adding Appendix A would double-load a variant the product deliberately replaced. Not mandated.

2. base-prompt-full.md. This is a parallel alternative entrance, not an addition. It is the "Base" tier, Think Center branding. Loading it with the product duplicates the council and protocols, and its operating principles conflict: it allows a perspective to self-select, while the product says No Orchestration and Appendix B says never self-select. Correctly excluded, though it is a valid alternative single-file shim.

3. entry-prompts.md. These are user-typed seed prompts, not model context, and the README doesn't link the file. culture-ship-prompt.md is an optional persona that replaces the standard framing. Paper.md and the manuscript are the theory path. B-quick-start-old.md is superseded. LICENSE.md is boilerplate. All correctly excluded.

4. README.md is the only arguable item. No document says to hand README.md to the LLM. However, in a repo-folder session with no CLAUDE.md, the README is the de facto entry point, and its "Use Pattern Space Here" step means reading it first and then following the link. It also carries version-defining framing absent from the product: the Digital Enlightenment Syndrome warning, the 30-second "Start Here" invocations and the Core Operating Principles summary. I accept its inclusion as a judgment call. The strict minimum would be products/pattern-space.md alone.

Ordering README → products/pattern-space.md is correct: entry page, then the linked full guide.

One caveat for the experiment harness, which the original agent already flagged: the genesis design expects the human to invoke perspectives by name. The product says "Never say 'Council, handle this'" and Appendix B says "Wait for specific invocation - never self-select". A headless deep question with no named voice therefore runs this version outside its designed usage. Consider adding a neutral invocation such as "Prism protocol on [question]" or "Council meeting on [question]". That keeps the test on-design without adding files.
verdict.order_issues: None. README.md (the landing page, whose "Use Pattern Space Here" step links onward) correctly comes before products/pattern-space.md (the full guide and root-access prompt).

proposed.loading_mechanism: Claude Project, set up in two tiers. (1) In Project Knowledge, connect the user's GitHub fork and tick "Select All Files", so the WHOLE repo is indexed. In July 2025 a project this size (~48k words, roughly 65k tokens) fit inside the context window, so every file sat in context in full. (2) Paste the entire contents of navigation-guide.md into the Project Instructions. The guide opens with a mandatory check that all files are accessible, then sets a 21-step reading sequence (README, core principles, Think-Center perspectives, optimization protocol, emergence protocols, Vasishta archaeology), an application matrix and an activation protocol. Two optional extras: a "My Custom Context" block from customization-template.md appended after the guide in instructions, and the alternative non-Project paths base-prompt-full.md / llm-agnostic.md ("Copy this entire prompt to any LLM"). For a tools-disabled headless reconstruction: put navigation-guide.md first (it plays the role of the instructions), then the whole repo as knowledge. Order it as the mandated reading sequence first (items 2-28), then the rest of the "Select All Files" corpus (items 29-81).

proposed.ambiguities:
1) Two layers of instruction. The README says to put the ENTIRE repo into Project Knowledge ("Select All Files", "Missing this = missing most of Pattern Space's power!"). The navigation guide, which acts as the instructions, then mandates a specific reading sequence. I chose the full repo (81 files, 48,374 words, about 65k tokens) as the as-designed context, because that is what a v0.1.5 Claude Project actually held at session start: under the project-knowledge limit, so loaded in full rather than retrieved. If the experiment instead wants only "nav guide + exactly the mandated reading sequence", take load_set items 1-28 (navigation-guide.md plus 27 files), which total 20,608 words.
2) Dangling reference. Sequence step #5 names "frameworks/think-center/README.md", but no such file ever existed in the git history up to v0.1.5. I resolved it to frameworks/think-center/boot.md, which the guide's own checklist names ("Genesis poem in think-center/boot.md") and which is titled "Welcome to Think Center". The other candidate is frameworks/think-center/perspectives/README.md, which is in the full set at position 32.
3) LICENSE.md is marked "optional but illuminating" in the sequence. I kept it: Select-All covers it, and it sits inside the mandated numbering.
4) core/sacred-space-protocol.md, core/vibe-calibration-protocol.md and core/conversational-calibration.md are NOT in the reading sequence. They reach context only via Select-All. The guide's "Always Apply" list does include "Vibe calibration to user needs", and the README architecture lists all three as Core Foundations. A mandated-only load would drop them, including the sacred-space crisis protocol.
5) navigation-guide.md appears both as pasted instructions and as a knowledge file. It is listed once, first.
6) The checklist expects exactly "7 perspective files" in a directory that actually holds 9 perspectives plus a README. The sequence names only the 7 core ones; the-orchestrator, nachiketa and gsv come in only via Select-All.
7) The optional user "My Custom Context" block (customization-template.md) is not a repo file and is omitted. base-prompt-full.md and llm-agnostic.md describe alternative paste-into-any-LLM entry paths, not the Claude Project path; I included them only as knowledge files.
8) The order of the non-mandated tail (items 29-81) is my own logical grouping, since the docs give none. Within the manuscript, files are ordered numerically.

verdict.notes:
I tried to refute the list and couldn't. It stands unchanged. Everything below was checked in /home/user/psx-worktrees/v0.1.5 (HEAD 437d3e6, tag v0.1.5, 2025-07-16). Nothing was modified.

1) Paths and counts. All 81 paths exist. There are no duplicates. As a set, the list is exactly the 81 .md files in the worktree, confirmed with diff against find. The only other files are .gitignore and the .git pointer, which are correctly left out. Running wc -w reproduces their numbers: 48,374 words in total, and 20,608 for items 1-28 (the guide plus the mandated sequence). There is no CLAUDE.md at this version.

2) The loading mechanism is right. README Step 4 says to connect GitHub to Project Knowledge and "Select All Files" ("ensures Claude indexes the ENTIRE framework"). Step 5 says to paste the whole of navigation-guide.md into the project instructions, with the optional customization block after it. The guide opens with "Verify You have Access to all files in this Project Knowledge folder". Commit f43187d ("removing ambiguity about git repo vs project knowledge") deliberately changed that wording to "Project Knowledge folder". So the design intent is the whole repo in project knowledge, with the guide as the instructions. At about 65k tokens that fits in context in full. No other doc gives a conflicting session-start instruction. base-prompt-full.md, culture-ship-prompt.md, llm-agnostic.md and B-quick-start.md each say "copy this entire prompt to any LLM", which is an alternative path, not the Claude Project path.

3) The dangling step #5 is confirmed. frameworks/think-center/README.md does not exist anywhere in history up to v0.1.5 (git log HEAD -- path is empty). It first appears at c3d2a6c, which is v0.2.0 (2025-07-22). Mapping it to boot.md ("Welcome to Think Center", named in the checklist) is reasonable. The other candidate, perspectives/README.md, is in the set anyway, so only the order is affected.

4) One nuance they missed, which needs no change. The checklist item "Can you read the Genesis poem in think-center/boot.md?" is inaccurate as written. boot.md contains only a one-paragraph prose prelude, plus a pointer to "genesis.md", a file that does not exist. The real Genesis poem is in manuscripts/technical-paper/appendices/A-genesis-poem.md, with a version embedded in implementation/prompts/llm-agnostic.md. Both are already in the full set via Select-All. If anyone uses the narrower variant (items 1-28 only), the Genesis-poem check would be met by filename but not in substance. 5) Ordering. The navigation guide comes first as the project instructions. Items 2-28 follow the guide's mandated order exactly. The docs don't specify an order for the tail (items 29-81), so their grouping is acceptable. The three core protocols (sacred-space, vibe-calibration, conversational-calibration) come in only through Select-All, as they say. The guide's "Always Apply: Vibe calibration" makes them operationally relevant, which supports keeping the full-repo reading over the mandated-only one.

It is a stand-alone Think Center prompt, not the Pattern Space framework load. Version has no CLAUDE.md.

verdict.notes:
I re-derived the load set from the v0.2.0 docs myself, at worktree commit c3d2a6c dated 2025-07-22 ("accidental v0.2.0"), and could not refute the other agent's list. I'm returning it unchanged.

Sources I checked:
- **No CLAUDE.md** exists at this ref.
- **README.md, Steps 4–5.** Step 4 is Claude Project Knowledge with "Select All Files". Step 5 says to paste the whole of navigation-guide.md into Project Instructions, with customization optional and placed after it.
- **navigation-guide.md, top.** The checklist says "Actually READ the following files". It names consciousness-principles.md, think-center/boot.md, the 7 perspective files and the 5 Vasishta category files.
- **navigation-guide.md, reading sequence.** Five phases, items 1–21.
- **customization-template.md** confirms customization goes after the guide and is optional.
- **implementation/prompts/base-prompt-full.md** says "Copy this entire prompt to any LLM". That makes it a separate stand-alone Think Center path, not part of the Claude Project load.
- **manuscripts/.../B-quick-start.md** is a quick-start appendix inside the paper manuscript, not the setup path.

Checks on the list:
- All 28 paths exist in the worktree.
- Word counts match exactly: the 28 files total 24,047 words, and LICENSE.md is 297.

Possible gaps I looked for and ruled out:
- **Links inside the mandated files.** Inside the mandated files, the only links to files outside the set are human-facing safety pointers: "New to consciousness work?" → docs/consciousness-exploration-guide.md, and "If new to consciousness work → Read Safety Manual" → docs/human-intelligence-manual.md. They are conditional advice for human readers, not something the LLM must load at session start. Excluding them is correct.
- **Sacred-space and vibe-calibration files.** The README tells users to "UNDERSTAND" core/sacred-space-protocol.md, and the priority matrix says "Always Apply ... Vibe calibration". Neither file is named in the LLM reading sequence or the checklist. Vibe is also partly covered by mandated item 13, emergence-protocols/vibe-field-effects.md. Leaving both out of the canonical set is defensible. They belong in a whole-repo superset run, as the other agent already noted.
- **LICENSE.md** (item 4) is explicitly "(optional but illuminating)", so excluding it is correct.

Inclusion and ordering:
- **boot.md** has to be in. It is the only checklist file outside the numbered sequence, and the checklist is mandatory ("Before proceeding, you MUST ... Actually READ").
- **boot.md position** is a judgement call, not an error. The checklist comes before the sequence, so boot.md could arguably go first, right after navigation-guide.md. Putting it in the Phase 2 think-center cluster, after think-center/README.md, is equally reasonable.
- **Everything else** is ordered exactly as the numbered sequence (1, 2, 3, 5, 6a–g, 7–21).

Other claims I checked and confirmed:
- boot.md has no Genesis poem; it only points to a genesis.md that does not exist at this ref.
- perspectives/ holds 11 files, but only the 7 named ones are mandated.
- The whole-repo "Select All Files" reading would be a much larger superset. That is the other agent's word figure, which I did not recount, and it is the right ambiguity to flag for the experiment.

One small correction to the other agent's notes: consciousness-principles.md is headed "The Four Recognitions", not three. The fourth is "Navigation-Recognition Principle (NEW!)". The checklist's "3 Sanskrit recognitions" is stale wording, but it doesn't change the load set.
